name: ESP32-DevKitC V4 (ESP32-DevKitC-32E)
description: The reference classic-ESP32 board: WROOM-32E module (4 MB flash), USB-UART bridge, EN/BOOT buttons and 2x19 breadboard pins for about $10; pick it for Bluetooth Classic, DAC or the Ethernet MAC.
notes: Only a power LED (no user LED); the BOOT button (GPIO0) is the only user button.
D0-D3, CMD and CLK (GPIO6-11) are wired to the module flash and are not usable as GPIO, so 26 pins are really usable.
GPIO34-39 are input-only; ADC2 channels cannot be used while Wi-Fi is on; strapping pins are GPIO0, 2, 5, 12 (flash voltage) and 15.
Size includes the ~6 mm antenna overhang (PCB is 48.26 mm). Rows are 25.4 mm apart (1.0 in), wider than most breadboards leave room for.
Variants: -32E (4 MB), -VE (WROVER-E, 8 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM, GPIO16/17 used by PSRAM), -32UE/-VIE (external antenna connector).
